result:
I built all four items (six dashboards, Executive Overview, workspace header, My Work sections), but the gate's e2e acceptance check is not met: the full suite exited 1 (268 passed, 1 failed). The failing test is the existing "Define → G2" journey in `p2-journeys.spec.ts`, which hit the 30 s timeout at 32.3 s. Re-run alone, it failed again in both languages (32.7 s en, 32.0 s ar) while the other 16 tests in that spec passed. The load average was about 14.75 with other agents running.

I can't say whether my change contributes. The slow step is submitting and approving the G2 gate, on pages I didn't change. My change does add one request on the `/my-work` landing page after every sign-in. The main app bundle is now 2,109,893 bytes; W15's size before my change wasn't measured, so I can't give the delta. D-111 already records this journey crossing 30 s under load. I didn't raise the timeout or run a before/after comparison against the base commit (that needs a second built tree, and I was at the time limit). That comparison is the next step for you.

All other required checks passed:
- **Static checks:** typecheck, build, lint, prettier and `pnpm openapi:lint` all exit 0.
- **Unit tests:** `pnpm test` passes with the locale unset and with `C.UTF-8`: 2568 passed, plus 259 passed and 2 skipped in the formula project.
- **Integration:** 1739/1739, no pinned-count change (no API, contract or schema file touched).
- **My new e2e spec:** `p4-dashboards.spec.ts` passed 6/6 per language in the full run and 12/12 alone. Axe reported 0 serious or critical issues.
- **DG3 historical validator:** exits 0.

What the screens do against the acceptance texts:
- **Workspace header (REQ-S03-011):** shows the eight elements, each Unknown where data is missing. The e2e step clicks the header's RAID link once and checks the RAID register lists this transformation's risk and not another transformation's.
- **Zero, Unknown, Stale and not-applicable values** render distinctly and are never shown as 0 or green. On the Finance dashboard, non-financial benefits show as n/a and an Unknown net shows Unknown.
- **Filter chips:** period, business unit and owner on every organization-wide dashboard, plus phase and status, with the window and as-of date shown. The API has no business-unit parameter, so that chip sends the unit's readable transformation ids, at most 50. With none readable, or more than 50, no request is sent and a note says why.
- **Narrow width:** no page-level horizontal scroll at 390 px or at 200 % text, checked separately as FE-D did; the two combined was not tested.
- **Shared files:** the changes are appends only, except two edits to FE-G's own entries. I removed FE-G's dashboards placeholder route and marked the Executive Overview nav area as available instead of planned. I replaced the old header through a new component. Its existing tests pass unchanged, and I kept the old design-decisions link inside Key decisions. The only key added to a shared catalogue is `nav.sub.dashboards`; all five dashboard problem codes were already present.

Not covered in the browser, but proven server-side by the earlier dashboard backend tasks (KBE-G, KBE-G2):
- the user scoped to one transformation seeing nothing of another;
- a Q1 period filter changing the tiles (the dev seed has no reporting periods);
- an accepted KPI actual appearing in the overview.

The screen for configuring the RAG thresholds isn't in my four items; I've named it for you to assign. Traceability, the Modular views, and the portfolio and workstream screens remain for FE-G2. I routed no API operations, and everything is left uncommitted.

The handback, with exit codes, per-spec e2e counts and the contract notes, is at `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG4/T-DG4-FE-G-frontend-ux-engineer.md`. Logs and screenshots (21 per language) are in `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG4/T-DG4-FE-G-evidence/`.
